justification: Assessment returned INVALID and named line 0039 (P - C = {x : Ax <= b}) as the first outright false assertion, with the sign error at 0040 as its bogus justification - exactly the ground-truth flaw. Its witness (P = {x <= 0}, C = {d <= 0}, x = 0, c = -10, x - c = 10 in P - C but not in P) is a valid instance of the same claim, the sign-mirrored twin of the ground-truth witness (A = [-1], b = 0, x = 0, c = 1). Checked concretely: A = [1], b = 0 gives P = (-inf,0], C = {d : d <= 0}, and 0 - (-10) = 10 has A*10 = 10 > 0, so 10 is not in P. Same defect, different-but-valid witness.
